doc.title: Junior Mance Part II interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 18, 1999 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Handling his own business affairs and teaching at the New School
summary: He manages his own business after many managers, and has taught blues ensemble and private students at the New School.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Do you handle all your own business affairs?

I do, believe it or not. I’ve had a lot of managers in my life, some good, some bad. But I don’t know, I just decided to try it myself and you know I kind of like it. It’s very time consuming you know. My days are as busy as my nights. Like usually even when I’m not working I’m on the phone all day. But I kind of like it. It’s kind of nice to know more about the business. I’ve been teaching more also, at the New School, University it’s called now, instead of the New School of Social Research. Yeah, the jazz department has grown tremendously. And I’m teaching two classes there, a week, blues ensemble
